content_units: Family Game Night Shortlist

Here’s a ranked set of 7 board games that fit   6 players  , are generally   learnable in under 15 minutes  , finish in   under 90 minutes  , and work well for   mixed ages and mixed gaming experience  .
Ranked Board Game Comparison
Rank   Game   Player Count Fit   Complexity   Competitiveness   Replay Value   Why it suits this group
1   Codenames   Excellent at 6   Low   Team-based, moderate   High   Great for mixed ages because experienced players can help without taking over; team play keeps it social and low-pressure.
2   Ticket to Ride   Very good at 6   Low-Medium   Moderate   High   Easy turns, familiar goals, and enough strategy to keep adults engaged without overwhelming younger or newer players.
3   Sushi Go Party!   Excellent at 6   Low   Light-moderate   High   Fast rounds, simple card drafting, and playful scoring make it easy for both teens and older adults to enjoy.

4   Just One   Excellent at 6   Very Low   Cooperative   Medium-High   One of the easiest to teach; everyone plays together, which reduces frustration and helps shy or inexperienced players join in quickly.
5   King of Tokyo   Very good at 6   Low   High   Medium-High   Big, fun dice-rolling energy with simple choices; competitive but not too brain-burny, especially good for lively family groups.
6   6 nimmt!   Excellent at 6   Low   Light-moderate   High   Super quick to learn and play, with simultaneous reveal that keeps all 6 involved and minimizes downtime.

7   Azul   Good at 4, workable with 6 only by splitting tables   Low-Medium   Moderate   High   Excellent family game overall, but it does not natively fit 6 in one game, so it ranks lower for your exact group size.
Best Picks for This Age Range
Option 1:   Codenames     Best overall balance of teamwork, laughter, and low rules overhead   Strongest fit for 6 mixed-skill players
Option 2:   Ticket to Ride     Best if your family likes classic board-game feel with gentle strategy   Great cross-generational appeal
Option 3:   Just One     Best if you want the easiest teach and least stressful play   Cooperative and beginner-friendly
Group-Fit Notes
For a group spanning   ages 12 to 68  , the strongest choices are games that:
- keep turns short
- avoid rules-heavy exceptions
- let newer players stay competitive
- create fun interaction without harsh elimination
That makes   Codenames  ,   Just One  ,   Sushi Go Party!  , and   Ticket to Ride   the safest bets.
King of Tokyo   is best if your family enjoys louder, more direct competition.
Game-Night Setup Tips
- Start with   Just One   or   Codenames   if some players are casual.
- Choose   Ticket to Ride   if the group wants a more traditional board-game feel.
- Pick   Sushi Go Party!   or   6 nimmt!   if you want a faster, lighter first game.
- Save   King of Tokyo   for later in the evening if the group is in a playful, competitive mood.
Selection Context
I ranked these by your priorities in order:   fits 6 players well  ,   easy to learn  ,   under 90 minutes  , and   works across mixed experience levels  .
I placed games lower if they were weaker on the exact   6-player fit  , even if they are excellent family games overall.
